question: On a particular take-off, you can accept up to 10 knots tailwind. The runway QDM is 047, the variation is 17E and the ATIS gives the wind direction as 210. What is the maximum wind strength you can accept?
explanation: ATIS winds are magnetic, so compare 210°M with runway 047°M: angle 163°. Tailwind = W × cos 17° → W = 10 / 0.956 ≈ 10.5 → 11 kt (anything stronger exceeds the limit).

question: Given: Magnetic heading = 255° VAR = 40° W GS = 375 kt W/V = 235° (T) / 120 kt Calculate the drift angle?
explanation: HDG(T) = 255 − 40 = 215°. The wind (235°) is 20° to the right of the nose, so drift is left. Solving the triangle with GS 375 kt gives TAS ≈ 485 kt and drift ≈ 6–7° left.

question: You are flying 090° C heading. Deviation is 2° W and Variation is 12 E. Your TAS is 160 knots. You are flying the 070 radial outbound from a VOR and you have gone 14 nm in 6 minutes. What is the W/V?
explanation: HDG(T) = 090 − 2 + 12 = 100°. Track = 070°M + 12 = 082°T, GS = 14 NM / 6 min = 140 kt. Solving gives W/V ≈ 158°/51 kt — only option A has the right direction (the speed in the option appears misprinted; compare the identical question that gives 160°/50).

question: Given: TAS = 140 kt HDG (T) = 005° W/V = 265/25kt Calculate the drift and GS?
explanation: Wind 265°/25 from the left-rear of heading 005° → drift right. CRP-5 / triangle: drift ≈ 10° R, GS ≈ 146 kt.

question: An aircraft is on final approach to runway 32R (322° ); The wind velocity reported by the tower is 350° /20 kt. TAS on approach is 95 kt. In order to maintain the centre line, the aircrafts heading (° M) should be:
explanation: Wind 350° is 28° right of the runway. Crosswind = 20 × sin 28° ≈ 9.4 kt. WCA = 9.4 / 95 × 60 ≈ 6° into wind → heading ≈ 328°.

question: If the wind is 010° T/100kts, variation is 30° W, the TAS is 400 kts and the aircraft is flying a heading of 100° M. What is the track and groundspeed?
explanation: HDG(T) = 100 − 30 = 070°. With 010°/100 kt the triangle gives track ≈ 084°T, GS ≈ 360 kt.

question: Given: True HDG = 035° TAS = 245 kt Track (T) = 046° GS = 220 kt Calculate the W/V?
explanation: Plotting HDG/TAS 035/245 and TR/GS 046/220 gives the wind vector ≈ 340°/51 kt.

question: Given: TAS = 170 kt HDG(T) = 100° W/V - 350/30kt Calculate the Track (° T) and GS?
explanation: Wind 350° from the left of heading 100° → drift right ≈ 9°, track ≈ 109°, GS ≈ 182 kt.

question: Given: TAS = 470 kt True HDG = 317° W/V = 045° (T)/45kt Calculate the drift angle and GS
explanation: Wind 045° is from the right-front of 317° → drift left ≈ 5°, GS ≈ 470 kt.

question: The reported surface wind from the control tower is 240° /35 kt. Runway 30 (300° ). What is cross-wind component?
explanation: Angle = 60°. Crosswind = 35 × sin 60° ≈ 30 kt.

question: An airfield has two runways, 05/23 and 30/12. The surface wind is given as 250° /30. The headwind component on 23 and the crosswind component on runway 30 will be:
explanation: RWY 23: angle 20° → headwind = 30 cos 20° ≈ 28 kt. RWY 30: angle 50° → crosswind = 30 sin 50° ≈ 23 kt.

question: Given: TAS = 135 kt HDG (° T) = 278 W/V = 140/20kt Calculate the Track (° T) and GS?
explanation: Wind 140° from right-rear of 278° → drift right ≈ 5°, track ≈ 283°, GS ≈ 150 kt.

question: Given: TAS = 472 kt True HDG = 005° W/V = 110° (T)/50kt Calculate the drift angle and GS?
explanation: Wind 110° from the right of heading 005° → drift left ≈ 6°, GS ≈ 487 kt.

question: Given: TAS = 205 kt HDG (T) = 180° W/V = 240/25kt Calculate the drift and GS?
explanation: Wind 240° from the right-front of 180° → drift left ≈ 6°, GS ≈ 194 kt.

question: Given: TAS = 90 kt HDG (T) = 355° W/V = 120/20kt Calculate the Track (° T) and GS?
explanation: Wind 120° from right-rear of 355° → drift left ≈ 9°, track ≈ 346°, GS ≈ 102 kt.

question: Given: Compass Heading 090° Deviation 2° W Variation 12° E TAS 160 kt Whilst maintaining a radial 070° from a VOR station, the aircraft flies a ground distance of 14 NM in 6 MIN. What is the W/V ° (T)?
explanation: HDG(T) = 090 − 2 + 12 = 100°, TAS 160. Track 070°M + 12 = 082°T, GS 140 kt. Triangle gives W/V ≈ 160°/50 kt.

question: Given: TAS = 132 kt HDG (T) = 053° W/V = 205/15kt Calculate the Track (° T) and GS?
explanation: Wind 205° from right-rear of 053° → drift left ≈ 3°, track ≈ 050°, GS ≈ 145 kt.

question: Given: TAS = 465 kt HDG (T) = 124° W/V = 170/80kt Calculate the drift and GS?
explanation: Wind 170° is 46° right of heading 124° → drift left ≈ 8°, GS ≈ 415 kt.

question: Given: TAS = 200 kt, Track (T) = 110° , W/V = 015/40kt. Calculate the HDG (° T) and GS?
explanation: Wind 015° from the left → steer left of track: HDG ≈ 099°T, GS ≈ 199 kt.

question: Given: TAS = 485 kt HDG (T) = 168° W/V = 130/75kt Calculate the Track (° T) and GS?
explanation: Wind 130° from the left-front of 168° → drift right ≈ 6°, track ≈ 174°, GS ≈ 428 kt.

question: Given: TAS = 155 kt Track (T) = 305° W/V = 160/18kt Calculate the HDG (° T) and GS?

question: Given: TAS = 220 kt Magnetic course = 212° W/V 160° (M)/ 50kt Calculate the GS?
explanation: Wind 160° is 52° left of course 212°: HDG ≈ 202°, GS ≈ 186 kt.

question: Construct the triangle of velocities on a piece of paper, showing the following data: TH 305, TAS 135 Kt, W/V 230/40, Period of time from 1130 to 1145. What is the GS in this period of time?
explanation: Wind 230° is 75° left-front of heading 305° → GS ≈ 130 kt.

question: Given: True course from A to B = 090° , TAS = 460 kt, W/V = 360/100kt, Average variation = 10° E, Deviation = - 2° . Calculate the compass heading and GS?
The wind velocity is 359/25. An aircraft is heading 180 at a TAS of 198 knots. (All directions are True). What is its track and groundspeed?
explanation: Almost a direct tailwind: track ≈ 179°, GS ≈ 223 kt.

question: Given: Runway direction 210° (M) Surface W/V 230° (M)/30kt Calculate the cross-wind component?

question: Given: TAS = 235 kt, HDG (T) = 076° W/V = 040/40kt Calculate the drift angle and GS?

question: Given: Course required = 085° (T) Forecast W/V 030/100kt TAS = 470 kt Distance = 265 NM Calculate the true HDG and flight time?
explanation: Wind 030° is 55° left of course → WCA ≈ 10° left: HDG ≈ 075°T, GS ≈ 405 kt. Time = 265/405 h ≈ 39 min.

question: Given: Runway direction 083° (M) Surface W/V 035/35kt. Calculate the effective headwind component?
explanation: Angle between wind 035° and runway 083° = 48°: headwind = 35 × cos 48° ≈ 23–24 kt.

question: Given: TAS = 375 kt True HDG = 124° W/V = 130° (T)/55kt. Calculate the true track and GS?
explanation: Wind 130° nearly on the nose (6° right) → drift ≈ 1° left: track ≈ 123°, GS ≈ 320 kt.

question: Given: TAS = 125 kt True HDG = 355° W/V = 320° (T)/30kt. Calculate the true track and GS?
explanation: Wind 320° from the left-front → drift right ≈ 10°: track ≈ 005°, GS ≈ 102 kt.

question: Given: TAS = 270 kt True HDG = 270° Actual wind 205° (T)/30kt Calculate the drift angle and GS?

explanation: HDG 054/450 and TR/GS 059/416 give W/V ≈ 010°/50 kt (drift 5° R, 34 kt headwind component).

question: Given: TAS = 270 kt Track (T) = 260° W/V = 275/30kt Calculate the HDG (° T) and GS?

question: Given: TAS = 200 kt Track (T) = 073° W/V = 210/20kt. Calculate the HDG (° T) and GS?
explanation: Wind 210° from the right-rear → steer right ≈ 4°: HDG ≈ 077°T, GS ≈ 214 kt.

question: Given: TAS = 465 kt Track (T) = 007° W/V = 300/80kt Calculate the HDG (° T) and GS?
explanation: Wind 300° from the left → steer left ≈ 9°: HDG ≈ 358°T, GS ≈ 428 kt.

question: For a given track the: Wind component = 45 kt Drift angle = 15° left TAS = 240 kt What is the wind component on the reverse track?
explanation: Crosswind = 240 × sin 15° ≈ 62 kt; GS on given track ≈ 240 cos 15° + 45 ≈ 277 kt. On the reverse track: 240 cos 15° − 45 = 187 kt → component ≈ −53 kt.

question: Given: AD = Air distance GD = Ground distance TAS = True Airspeed GS = Groundspeed Which of the following is the correct formula to calculate ground distance (GD) gone?
explanation: Ground distance / air distance = GS / TAS → GD = AD × GS / TAS.

question: Given: M 0.80 OAT -50° C FL 330 GS 490 kt VAR 20° W Magnetic heading 140° Drift is 11° Right Calculate the true W/V?
Given: True HDG = 002° TAS = 130 kt Track (T) = 353° GS = 132 kt Calculate the W/V?
explanation: HDG 002/130 and TR/GS 353/132 give W/V ≈ 093°/21 kt → closest 095°/20 kt.

question: Given: FL120 OAT is ISA standard CAS is 200 kt Track is 222° (M) Heading is 215° (M) Variation is 15° W. Time to fly 105 NM is 21 MIN. What is the W/V?
explanation: TAS at FL120 ISA, CAS 200 ≈ 239 kt. HDG 215°M = 200°T, track 207°T, GS 105 NM/21 min = 300 kt → W/V ≈ 050°(T)/70 kt.

question: Given: TAS = 227 kt Track (T) = 316° W/V = 205/15kt Calculate the HDG (° T) and GS?
explanation: Wind 205° from the left-rear → steer left ≈ 3–4°: HDG ≈ 312°T, GS ≈ 232 kt.

question: If the wind is 230° T/50 kts variation is 20° W and the TAS is 230 kts. What true heading is required to fly a true track of 025° ?
explanation: Wind 230° comes from the left-rear of track 025°, so steer about 5° left into it: HDG ≈ 020°T (variation is not needed for a true heading).

question: Given: True HDG = 145° TAS - 240 kt Track (T) - 150° GS - 210 kt Calculate the W/V?

question: Required course 045T, W/V = 190 /30, FL = 55 at ISA, Variation = 15E. CAS = 120 knots. What is mag heading and G/S?
explanation: TAS at FL55 ISA, CAS 120 ≈ 130 kt. Course 045°T, wind 190/30 → HDG ≈ 052.6°T − 15E = 037.6°M, GS ≈ 154 kt.

question: Given: True Heading = 090° TAS = 200 kt W/V = 220° / 30 kt Calculate the GS?

question: Given: Maximum allowable crosswind component is 20 kt. Runway 06, RWY QDM 063° (M). Wind direction 100° (M) Calculate the maximum allowable windspeed?
explanation: Angle 37°: max wind = 20 / sin 37° ≈ 33 kt.

question: Given: Course 040° (T), TAS is 120 kt, Wind speed 30 kt. Maximum drift angle will be obtained for a wind direction of:
explanation: Drift is maximum when the wind is at 90° to the heading, i.e. ≈ 104.5° from track (90° + 14.5° max drift): 040 + 104.5 ≈ 145°.

question: Given: TAS = 250 kt HDG (T) = 029° W/V = 035/45kt Calculate the drift and GS?

explanation: Course 045°M = 060°T. TAS ≈ 130 kt; wind 190/30 → HDG ≈ 070°T = 055°M, GS ≈ 147 kt.

question: Pressure Altitude is 27,000 feet, OAT = -35C, Mach No = 0.45, W/V = 270/85, Track = 200T. What is drift and groundspeed?
Given: TAS = 225 kt, HDG (° T) - 123° W/V - 090/60kt Calculate the Track (° T) and GS?
explanation: Wind 090° from the left-front → drift right ≈ 11°: track ≈ 134°, GS ≈ 178 kt.

question: Given: Maximum allowable tailwind component for landing 10 kt. Planned runway 05 (047° magnetic). The direction of the surface wind reported by ATIS 210° . Variation is 17° E. Calculate the maximum allowable windspeed that can be accepted without exceeding the tailwind limit?
explanation: ATIS wind 210°M vs RWY 047°M: 163° off the nose. Max wind = 10/cos 17° ≈ 10.5 → 11 kt.

question: Given: TAS = 440 kt HDG (T) = 349° W/V = 040/40kt Calculate the drift and GS?
explanation: Wind 040° from the right-front → drift left ≈ 4°, GS ≈ 415 kt.

question: The following information is displayed on an Inertial Navigation System: GS 520 kt, True HDG 090° , Drift angle 5° right, TAS 480 kt. SAT (static air temperature) -51° C. The W/V being experienced is:

question: An aircraft is at ROK (N55° 58.1 E025° 36.1) at 2057 UTC, FL180, heading 017° M, TAS 120 kts. Routing via UH133 it is at LBN (N56° 46.4 E026° 21.1) at 2120 UTC. What mean wind velocity has affected the aircraft?
explanation: ROK → LBN ≈ 027°T, 54 NM in 23 min → GS ≈ 142 kt. With HDG 017°M ≈ 023°T (variation ≈ 6°E on the chart) and TAS 120, W/V ≈ 228°/24 kt → 230°/25 kt.

question: Given: Half way between two reporting points the navigation log gives the following information: TAS 360 kt, W/V 330° /80kt, Compass heading 237° , Deviation on this heading -5° , Variation 19° W. What is the average ground speed for this leg?

question: Given: TAS = 198 kt HDG (° T) = 180 W/V = 359/25. Calculate the Track(° T) and GS?

explanation: Minimum: headwind 10 = W cos 60° → W = 20 kt. Maximum: crosswind 35 = W sin 60° → W ≈ 40 kt.

question: Given: True HDG = 133° TAS = 225 kt Track (T) = 144° GS = 206 kt Calculate the W/V?
